# **Exhaustive Methodological Critique and Adjudicated Specification: NAICS Hyperbolic Embedding System**

## **Architectural and Theoretical Context**

The ambition to embed the 2022 North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) into a hyperbolic space (specifically, the Lorentz model) represents a sophisticated attempt to leverage non-Euclidean geometry for hierarchical representation learning. The core premise—that the exponential volume growth of hyperbolic space naturally accommodates the exponentially expanding leaf nodes of a hierarchical taxonomy—is theoretically sound and well-supported by foundational literature regarding representation tradeoffs for hierarchical data (Sala et al., 20181; Nickel & Kiela, 20173). The methodology proposes a decoupled, two-stage architecture: an inductive, text-conditioned contrastive encoder (the text stage, S2) followed by a transductive graph-convolutional refinement process (the graph stage, S3), evaluated ultimately on structural taxonomy reconstruction (S4).  
However, a rigorous examination of the mathematical formulations, architectural composition, and objective functions reveals that the system operates in an architectural uncanny valley. It attempts to utilize advanced geometric concepts but relies heavily on outdated approximation techniques, inert curriculum mechanisms, and misaligned optimization targets. The methodology ignores several critical advancements in fully hyperbolic neural networks, robust semantic similarity measurement, and geometry-task alignment that have defined the state of the art over the past several years.

### **The Shift to Fully Hyperbolic Architectures**

Historically, early hyperbolic graph neural networks operated by mapping features from the hyperbolic manifold to a Euclidean tangent space (typically at the origin), applying standard Euclidean operations such as linear transformations, message passing, or normalizations, and subsequently projecting the aggregated features back to the manifold via exponential maps (Chami et al., 20195). The reviewed graph stage (S3) relies entirely on this outdated "tangent-space" approach. The published state of the art has decisively moved toward fully hyperbolic neural networks (Chen et al., 20216; Shimizu et al., 20206).  
Modern theoretical frameworks recognize that tangent-space approximations severely distort intrinsic geometric properties. Most notably, transformations in the Euclidean tangent space warp the radial coordinate, which is the exact property responsible for encoding hierarchical depth in the Poincaré and Lorentz models. Recent literature demonstrates that utilizing intrinsic Lorentz transformations—such as Lorentz multinomial logistic regression, Gyrogroup batch normalization, and Busemann functions—circumvents the severe distortion and numerical instability inherent in tangent-space mapping (Chen et al., 20268). By ignoring fully hyperbolic building blocks, the reviewed methodology structurally neutralizes the geometric properties it aims to refine.

### **High-Dimensional Boundary Saturation**

The text stage (S2) maps the textual descriptions of NAICS codes into a 384-dimensional hyperbolic space, applying a strict norm cap. The methodology explicitly notes that historical runs saturated at this cap. This is a known pathology in the literature. As dimensionality increases, the volume of a hyperbolic space concentrates exponentially at its boundary, leading to severe norm saturation where embeddings push to the maximum allowed radius (Guo et al., 202310; Van Nooten & Daelemans, 202511). When constrained by a norm cap in high dimensions (e.g., ![][image1]), hyperbolic embeddings succumb to boundary crowding. The intended radial encoding of the taxonomy collapses into a purely angular distribution on the cap boundary, functionally reducing the hyperbolic space to a Euclidean hypersphere. Consequently, the hyperbolic distance collapses into a monotonic function of the spherical angle. The reviewed methodology ignores high-dimensional boundary crowding solutions, such as radius-aware objective scaling, intrinsic Busemann margins, or dimension-adaptive curvature.

### **Geometry-Task Alignment and Taxonomy Expansion**

The evaluation protocol (S4) exclusively measures the reconstruction of the training target, specifically the structural distance matrix ![][image2]. The state of the art in taxonomy embedding evaluates representations based on taxonomy expansion capabilities and downstream task alignment (Shen et al., 202013; Naddeo et al., 202615). Recent analyses in geometric deep learning prove that a graph's inherent "hyperbolicity" is insufficient to guarantee that hyperbolic embeddings will outperform Euclidean ones; the downstream task itself must also align with hyperbolic geometry (Naddeo et al., 202615). By failing to evaluate out-of-sample taxonomy expansion or execute the proposed economic benchmarks, the methodology ignores the standard evidentiary requirements for representation learning, evaluating only the model's capacity to memorize the training distribution. Real-world applications of foundation models for geospatial and economic prediction rely heavily on downstream evaluation tasks, such as predicting urban function or economic output, to validate embedding utility (Li et al., 202417).

## **Structural Deficits and Theoretical Misalignments**

The current reference configuration contains severe mathematical and architectural flaws. The following enumerated critique points (C1 through C15) represent critical failures in the methodology, supported by current geometric deep learning and computational linguistics literature. These points form the basis of the final adjudicated specification.

### **C1: Geometric Collapse via the Norm Cap**

In the text stage (S2), the tangent vector ![][image3] is capped such that its Euclidean norm never exceeds ![][image4]. Consequently, every point ![][image5] lies within a closed geodesic ball of radius 2\. As noted in the methodology, high-dimensional spaces (![][image1]) cause points to push outward, sitting exactly on the cap boundary where ![][image6].  
When all points sit on the boundary cap, the radius ![][image7] becomes a constant across the entire embedding space. In the Lorentz model, the distance ![][image8] between two points on the same radius reduces to a monotonic function of the Euclidean angle ![][image9] between their spatial directions. The consequence is absolute: the model completely loses its ability to encode hierarchical depth, which mathematically requires varying radii. The level alignment loss (![][image10]) receives zero meaningful gradient because the radius cannot adjust. The hyperbolic space acts entirely as a standard Euclidean hypersphere, negating the foundational premise of the methodology. This is an extensively documented failure in high-dimensional hyperbolic networks (Guo et al., 202310; Van Nooten & Daelemans, 202511).

### **C2: Tangent-Space Layer Normalization Erases Depth**

The graph stage (S3) maps points to the tangent space at the origin via the logarithmic map ![][image11], applies a message-passing aggregate based on attention scores, and then applies a standard Layer Normalization (![][image12]) before projecting the vector back to the manifold via the exponential map ![][image13].  
This sequence is mathematically fatal to hyperbolic hierarchies. Standard Layer Normalization centers and scales a vector such that its variance is 1\. In an ![][image14]\-dimensional tangent space, this forces the Euclidean norm of the normalized tangent vector to be approximately ![][image15]. The Riemannian exponential map ![][image16] takes a tangent vector ![][image17] and maps it to a point on the hyperboloid with a radius directly proportional to ![][image18]. Because Layer Normalization standardizes ![][image18], the radius of the point after the ![][image13] map is determined entirely by the Layer Normalization gain parameter and the ambient dimension. This completely and irreversibly destroys whatever radial coordinate (and thus, whatever hierarchical depth) was learned in S2 or the previous graph layer. This explains the methodological observation that ![][image19] reaches ![][image20] after two layers at 385 dimensions. Tangent-space normalization is recognized as mathematically incoherent for hyperbolic networks; modern systems rely exclusively on Gyrogroup Batch Normalization or purely intrinsic Riemannian normalization to preserve radial semantics (Chen et al., 20268).  
![][image21]

### **C3: Dimensional and Transductive Disconnect**

The architectural composition between the text stage (S2) and the graph stage (S3) is fundamentally broken. S2 is an inductive text encoder mapping raw text to ![][image22]. S3 treats node states as free parameters initialized at ![][image23], but operates under a reference configuration of ![][image24]. There is no projection, pooling, or lifting map defined between ![][image22] and ![][image24]. The composition is mathematically undefined as configured.  
Furthermore, because S3 optimizes free parameters transductively (updating node states directly rather than updating an encoder), a new NAICS code or a novel business description can only be processed by the S2 inductive encoder. Because S2's geometry and S3's geometry immediately diverge during S3 training (since no gradients flow back to the text encoder), the system produces two misaligned embedding spaces. The transductive refinement is entirely incompatible with the stated primary goal of using textual business descriptions as downstream queries.

### **C4: Domination of Cross-Sector Targets in Distance Matching**

The structural distance target ![][image2] assigns a tree-based path distance for within-sector pairs (ranging from 0.5 to 8.0) but assigns an arbitrary constant scalar of ![][image25] to all cross-sector pairs. Statistically, 87.9% of all possible pairs in the NAICS taxonomy cross sectors.  
Because S2 utilizes a Mean Squared Error (MSE) distance-matching loss (![][image26]), the squared penalty for a slight proportional deviation on a ![][image27] target dwarfs any gradient derived from fine-grained within-sector taxonomy sorting (![][image28]). The continuous hyperbolic space is forced by the optimizer to solve a crude binary classification problem (same sector versus different sector) rather than building a nuanced hierarchy. The S4 evaluation statistics (Pearson correlation, NDCG) are completely corrupted by this point-biserial distribution, making them insensitive to local hierarchical accuracy. Using arbitrary extreme scalar limits rather than probabilistic Information Content (IC) to define cross-tree semantic similarity violates established taxonomic similarity practices (Resnik, 199518).

### **C5: Sparse Mixture of Experts on Empty Placeholders**

The text stage utilizes a Sparse Mixture of Experts (MoE) over four channels (Title, Description, Illustrative Examples, Exclusion Text). However, the "illustrative examples" channel is empty for 49.4% of the codes, and the "exclusion text" channel is empty for 47.6% of the codes. The methodology replaces these empty channels with a constant placeholder string ![][image29].  
Pushing a static placeholder string through a 6-layer transformer and an adapter to generate a dense vector, and then allowing an MoE router to dynamically evaluate and weight this vector, is highly inefficient and prone to routing collapse. Because the placeholder is deterministically present based on the hierarchical level of the code (e.g., levels 2-4 never have examples), the placeholder creates a spurious correlation. The MoE router learns to use the presence of the static string ![][image29] to leak the level of the code to the embedding, bypassing the textual semantics entirely.

### **C6: Contradictory Gradients on Lineal Kinship**

The S1 sampler generates negative candidates for sibling anchors using their grandchildren. The decoupled contrastive loss (![][image30]) treats these grandchildren as negatives and pushes them away from the anchor. Simultaneously, the structural preference loss (![][image31]) orders candidates by structural distance ![][image2]. Because the target distance dictates that grandchildren (![][image32]) are strictly closer to the anchor than siblings (![][image33]), the preference loss pulls the grandchildren inward relative to the sibling positive. The optimizer is subjected to directly contradictory gradients on the same tuple, destabilizing the manifold layout.

### **C7: Misalignment of Exclusion Semantics**

Explicit exclusion cross-references within the NAICS text represent critical boundary markers between industries. S2 respects this, treating explicit exclusions as mandatory, reserved hard negatives that repel each other. However, S3 relies on a structural taxonomy graph where explicitly excluded pairs are ignored in edge construction. Consequently, structurally adjacent excluded pairs (such as the 474 sibling pairs that explicitly exclude one another) are treated as standard positive message-passing neighbors in S3. The graph stage explicitly pulls together the exact pairs the text stage was trained to push apart.

### **C8 through C15: Inert Mechanisms and Evaluation Fragility**

The methodology contains extensive designed elements that are mathematically inert under execution, creating immense technical debt.

* **C8:** Evaluative circularity exists because the system trains on ![][image2] and validates on ![][image2], testing memorization rather than representation quality.  
* **C9:** As noted in C6, lineal positive pairs acting as negatives cause metric collapse.  
* **C10:** Unaligned spatial dimensions break S2-S3 composition entirely.  
* **C11:** NDCG graded relevance is strictly point-biserial due to ![][image27].  
* **C12:** The contrastive loss log-sum-exp excludes the positive, causing it to be unbounded below.  
* **C13:** Validation loss is strictly in-sample, drawing from the same pool of 1,273 anchors used in training, masking overfitting.  
* **C14:** S4 thresholds for refinement acceptance are arbitrary constants rather than statistically significant margins.  
* **C15:** Setting curvature ![][image34] globally hardcodes the metric, rendering the system fragile if curvature is ever treated as a learnable parameter.

## **Prioritized Remediation and System Improvements**

The following improvements are ranked by expected value and categorized by their methodological nature, moving from critical mathematical fixes to architectural upgrades and scope extensions.

### **Category 1: Fix Errors (Critical Interventions)**

| Priority | Remediation Target | Technical Implementation | Addressed Critique |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **1** | Abolish the S2 Norm Cap | Remove the hard limit at ![][image35]. To prevent numerical explosion in the Lorentz model, utilize mathematically sound Busemann function formulations for margins (Chen et al., 20268) or apply a soft, learned radius penalty that passes continuous gradients. | C1 |
| **2** | Replace Tangent-Space LayerNorm | Completely remove the ![][image12] in the tangent space of S3. Replace it with a Riemannian Batch Normalization (GyroBN) layer that operates intrinsically on the manifold, allowing the network to standardize feature distributions without projecting out the radial depth (Chen et al., 202620). | C2 |
| **3** | Resolve Dimensional Mismatch | Force S2 and S3 to operate in the same ambient dimension. If dimension reduction is strictly required for S3, define a formal, differentiable hyperbolic projection matrix layer between the S2 text output and S3 node initialization. | C3, C10 |
| **4** | Fix Target Distance Scaling | Discard the hardcoded ![][image36]. Implement a dynamic, data-driven cross-sector penalty, or utilize Information Content (IC) path scores that scale non-linearly based on the probability of encountering a hierarchical instance in the corpus (Resnik, 199518). | C4, C11 |
| **5** | Repair Exclusion Topology | Harmonize exclusion semantics across stages. If S2 treats exclusions as repulsive negatives, S3 must model them as negative edges (utilizing signed graph convolution techniques) rather than standard message-passing neighbors. | C7 |

### **Category 2: Adopt Better Methods (Architectural Upgrades)**

| Priority | Remediation Target | Technical Implementation | Addressed Critique |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **6** | Unified Inductive Architecture | Instead of a decoupled transductive graph stage (S3), adopt an inductive Hyperbolic Graph Attention Network (HGAT). Pass the text embeddings ![][image23] as node features into the GNN and backpropagate the GNN loss entirely through the frozen sentence encoder's adapters. This guarantees that new textual queries can be mapped directly into the refined graph topology. | C3, C13 |
| **7** | Mask Empty Channels in MoE | Remove the placeholder string ![][image29]. If a channel is empty, pass a zero-vector and strictly mask it out of the MoE gating network (forcing ![][image37] before the softmax). This prevents the router from wasting capacity on static noise and prevents hierarchical level-leakage. | C5 |
| **8** | Unify the Objective Function | A six-term objective in S2 (with inert terms) is unjustified. The literature recommends a single, unified hierarchy-aware contrastive loss. Adopt Hyperbolic Entailment Cones for contrastive loss, which naturally bounds parent-child representations without explicit distance matching (Ganea et al., 201822). | C6, C8 |
| **9** | Prune Inert Mechanisms | Remove the 3-phase curriculum, false-negative clustering, and geometric routing. Code that executes but mathematically cannot alter the tensor state adds significant technical debt without algorithmic benefit. | C8 |

### **Category 3: Extend Scope (Evaluation and Applicability)**

| Priority | Remediation Target | Technical Implementation | Addressed Critique |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **10** | Extrinsic Downstream Evaluation | The current acceptance gate (S4) measures self-reconstruction. Expand the scope to execute the defined economic benchmark (Ridge regression on employment statistics) immediately. This aligns with the necessity of testing geometry-task alignment (Naddeo et al., 202615). | C8 |
| **11** | Taxonomy Expansion Benchmark | Adopt a Taxonomy Expansion benchmark to prove true generalization (Shen et al., 202013). Hold out 10% of leaf nodes during training and query the system to predict their optimal parent placement using only textual embeddings. | C13 |
| **12** | Statistical Significance Gating | Replace the arbitrary constant thresholds in the S4 acceptance gate with paired statistical significance tests (e.g., a paired t-test on NDCG improvement across batches) to ensure that graph refinement provides reliable, non-spurious gains over the text stage. | C14 |

## **Resolution of Methodological Open Questions**

The methodological description poses seven explicit open questions for the reviewer. The synthesized answers below resolve these inquiries based on state-of-the-art computational and geometric literature.  
**1\. Where does the overall design sit relative to the state of the art in taxonomy embedding, hierarchical text classification, and taxonomy expansion? Is there a simpler design that dominates it?** The current design is structurally disjointed and relies on outdated tangent-space approximations. The state of the art for hierarchical text classification and taxonomy expansion is a unified, end-to-end Hyperbolic Graph Attention Network (HGAT). In this dominating architecture, textual representations serve as node features and are updated via intrinsic Lorentz attention, trained inductively. The current transductive graph refinement over unaligned dimensions is stale and actively hinders the goal of out-of-sample query matching.  
**2\. Is hyperbolic geometry justified for a 2,125-node, five-level taxonomy embedded in 384 dimensions, given that the realized representation is confined to a sphere of fixed radius?** Hyperbolic geometry is highly justified for the NAICS taxonomy, but *not* in 384 dimensions. In ultra-high dimensions, exponential volume growth forces embeddings to the manifold boundary, resulting in spherical collapse (the fixed radius observed in the historical run). If 384 dimensions are strictly required to capture textual nuances, a Euclidean or spherical manifold is actually preferred to avoid this saturation (Van Nooten & Daelemans, 202511). To leverage hyperbolic advantages, append a dimensionality reduction head to the text encoder to map the representation down to a low-dimensional hyperbolic space (e.g., ![][image38]), where distortion and capacity tradeoffs are optimal (Sala et al., 20181).  
**3\. Is it defensible to supervise with, and evaluate against, the same structural target?** It is methodologically indefensible. Training on structural distance ![][image2] and validating by evaluating Pearson correlation with ![][image2] on the exact same codes guarantees severe overfitting and evaluates memorization, not representation quality. Valid independent signals must include out-of-sample taxonomic placement (Taxonomy Expansion) or downstream economic utility (Geometry-Task Alignment).  
**4\. How should explicit exclusions be treated consistently across the two stages?** Explicit exclusions denote rigid semantic boundaries. They must be treated as hard, repulsive negatives in the contrastive loss of the text stage, and they must be explicitly modeled as negative (repulsive) edges in any graph-based refinement matrix. Allowing structurally adjacent but explicitly excluded codes to pass positive messages corrupts the manifold.  
**5\. Which inert or nominal mechanisms should be repaired, and which removed?** The norm cap must be removed to repair the radius penalty and prevent spherical collapse. The tangent-space LayerNorm must be replaced with GyroBN. The placeholder ![][image29] strings, the inert 3-phase curriculum, the false-negative clustering, and the graph-curriculum filters should be entirely removed as they introduce technical debt without altering the tensor state. The learnable curvature is currently nominal due to the cap; it should be repaired and constrained to adapt natively across all distance functions.  
**6\. What is the minimal experiment that would decide whether the graph stage should exist at all?** Execute a strict Taxonomy Expansion task by holding out 20% of leaf nodes from all training stages. Compare the Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR) of predicting their correct parent using only the text-stage embeddings ![][image23] versus the transductive graph states ![][image39] (mapped via a learned projection). If ![][image39] does not statistically significantly improve MRR, the graph stage provides zero inductive value and should be deprecated.  
**7\. For the stated uses, what estimand should replace structural reconstruction, and what does that imply for the objective?** The correct estimand is Downstream Task Alignment (Naddeo et al., 202615). This implies that the objective should optimize for the ![][image40] of the economic prediction benchmark or the retrieval NDCG against an independent dataset of real-world establishment descriptions. The loss function should pivot away from absolute distance matching (![][image26]) and focus on ranking and hierarchical entailment.

## **Adjudicated Critique Ledger**

The following ledger records the final, adjudicated positions reached regarding the methodology. First-pass findings that were challenged have been updated to reflect the final architectural consensus.

| ID | Critique Topic | Adjudicated Position & Reason |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **C1** | High-dimensional norm cap causes boundary saturation and loss of radial depth. | **Accepted.** The hard cap will be removed. A soft, differentiable radius penalty will be implemented to prevent numerical explosion in the Lorentz model. |
| **C2** | Tangent-Space LayerNorm in S3 projects out the radial coordinate. | **Accepted.** The designer initially pushed back, citing training instability without normalization. It was agreed to replace the operation with intrinsic Riemannian Batch Normalization (GyroBN). |
| **C3** | Transductive S3 creates disconnected, out-of-sample mapping failures. | **Accepted.** Agreed to transition S3 to an inductive formulation, allowing gradient flow back to the S2 text adapters. |
| **C4** | **![][image36]** dominates MSE loss, collapsing within-sector hierarchies. | **Accepted.** Cross-sector pairs will be masked out of ![][image26] and handled solely by the contrastive ranking loss. Information Content (IC) will be explored for future metric scaling. |
| **C5** | Sparse MoE over 50% empty text channels causes routing inefficiency. | **Accepted.** The placeholder string ![][image29] will be removed in favor of strict attention masking for missing channels to prevent level-leakage. |
| **C6** | Lineal positive pairs (grandchildren) act as negatives for sibling anchors, causing contradictory forces. | **Accepted.** Negative mining generation rules will be updated to exclude all lineal descendants from acting as valid negatives for collateral pairs. |
| **C7** | Exclusions are ignored in S3 graph edges, causing gradient contradictions. | **Accepted without pushback.** Excluded pairs will be treated as negative (repulsive) edges in the graph topology. |
| **C8** | Evaluative circularity (Testing on ![][image2] after training on ![][image2]). | **Rejected.** The designer argued that structural reconstruction is a necessary, non-negotiable sanity check for internal taxonomy consistency. **Compromise:** The metric is retained as a gate, but the downstream economic benchmark will be elevated to the primary Key Performance Indicator (KPI). |
| **C9** | Inert 3-phase negative mining curriculum adds dead code. | **Accepted without pushback.** The curriculum controller and geometric routing modules will be stripped from the reference configuration. |
| **C10** | Unaligned spatial dimensions (![][image1] vs ![][image41]) breaks S2-S3 composition. | **Accepted without pushback.** A linear projection matrix will be added to the S3 initialization sequence to bridge the dimensional gap. |
| **C11** | Evaluation NDCG relevance grades are point-biserial due to ![][image27]. | **Accepted.** NDCG graded relevance will be recalibrated using continuous Information Content (IC) path scores rather than the flat ![][image27] distance. |
| **C12** | Contrastive loss log-sum-exp excludes positive, unbounded below. | **Rejected.** The designer stated this formulation specifically follows decoupled contrastive learning standards to prevent positive-pair loss saturation. The formulation is retained as-is. |
| **C13** | Validation loss is strictly in-sample. | **Accepted.** A true holdout set (20% of leaf nodes) will be established to measure out-of-sample taxonomy expansion capabilities. |
| **C14** | S4 thresholds for refinement acceptance are arbitrary. | **Accepted.** Hardcoded thresholds will be replaced with paired statistical significance tests (e.g., paired t-test on NDCG improvement). |
| **C15** | Using ![][image34] hardcodes curvature, making distance formulas fragile. | **Accepted without pushback.** Curvature ![][image42] will be parameterized as a global, learnable tensor passed to all relevant distance functions. |
